title: How AI Model Weights Determine Compute Power
hook: Ever wondered why running an AI model like Llama 70B makes your GPU scream, while a 7B model runs effortlessly on a laptop? It all comes down to model weights.

sections.heading: What Are Weights?
sections.text: In modern AI, weights are the learned numerical parameters stored in memory that determine how neural activations flow. A 7-billion parameter model literally holds seven billion distinct floating point numbers.

sections.heading: The Memory Equation
sections.text: Here is the exact formula. At standard 16-bit precision, every single parameter requires two bytes of storage. That means a 70-billion parameter model demands a staggering 140 gigabytes of ultra-fast VRAM just to load the weights into GPU memory.

sections.heading: The Bandwidth Bottleneck
sections.text: During inference, text generation is strictly memory-bandwidth bound. For every single token generated, the GPU must stream every active weight from VRAM into the compute cores. More weights mean more gigabytes transferred per second.

sections.heading: Quantization Magic
sections.text: This is why quantization is revolutionary. By compressing weights from 16-bit down to 4-bit, we slash memory requirements by four times, enabling massive models to run on consumer hardware with virtually zero loss in intelligence.

cta: Now you know: model weight size and precision directly dictate your compute costs. Follow for more deep-dive AI engineering breakdowns!
seo_description: Learn how AI model weights and parameter counts determine the VRAM, compute power, and memory bandwidth needed to run large language models.
